# BYD confirms plan to unveil humanoid robot in August

[Phate Zhang](https://cnevpost.com/author/phate-zhang/) •  Jul 28, 2026 at 2:38 PM Asia/Shanghai 

[ 0 ](#comments) [ 17 ](javascript:void%280%29;)

![A humanoid robot and a robot dog on display at the Changan booth at the Shanghai Auto Show in April 2025.](https://cnevpost.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/2026072806354091.jpg) 

A humanoid robot and a robot dog on display at the Changan booth at the Shanghai Auto Show in April 2025\. Credit: CnEVPost
> * BYD told China Securities Journal it plans to unveil a humanoid robot in August.
> * One of BYD's offline experience centers previously posted a teaser image, hinting its first humanoid robot product will debut in early August.

[BYD](https://cnevpost.com/byd/) (HKEX: 1211) has confirmed it will unveil its first humanoid robot in August, becoming the latest Chinese automaker to move into the robotics race.

The Chinese new energy vehicle (NEV) maker told China Securities Journal on Tuesday that it plans to unveil a humanoid robot in August at its "Di Space."

Di Space is BYD's network of offline science education and experience venues. The WeChat account of its Zhengzhou venue [posted a humanoid robot teaser image](https://cnevpost.com/2026/07/26/byd-may-unveil-humanoid-robot-aug/) on July 25, hinting that its first humanoid robot product will debut in early August.

Join us on [Telegram](https://telegram.me/CnEVPost)  or [Google News](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?
q=cnevpost.com) 

The poster's description focused on interactive experience rather than technical specifications. "It won't show up with a pile of specs and jargon," the text read. "Maybe when you walk closer, it moves slightly."

Since Di Space is positioned around hands-on, interactive displays, the August event is expected to be the first public showing of a physical prototype rather than a concept announcement.

BYD executives have signaled the move several times before. Executive vice president Stella Li [said in a talk show](https://cnevpost.com/2026/06/03/byd-enters-humanoid-robot-market/) that the company was developing robots.

Li said the key to competition in robots lies in manufacturing capability along with software and hardware strength, and that automotive capabilities share the same roots as robotics technology.

She also said BYD plans to build an open platform that would produce both its own in-house robots and products co-developed with other companies.
BYD [set up a dedicated team](https://cnevpost.com/2024/12/26/byd-sets-up-lab-humanoid-robots-report/) in late 2024 to develop embodied artificial intelligence products, including humanoid robots, under its 15th Business Division, according to a local media report at the time.

Li said last month that she hopes every BYD store will eventually have two or three robots to introduce and demonstrate vehicles to customers. She expects robot sales advisors to be ready for real-world use in the next year or two.

Still, she said robots cannot replace the emotional connection between human salespeople and customers.

Chinese automakers moving into robotics has become a trend. Aimoga, a brand incubated by Chery, has already begun selling humanoid robots to consumers, while SAIC-GM has deployed wheeled humanoid robots on battery assembly lines. [Xpeng](https://cnevpost.com/xpeng/) (NYSE: XPEV) plans to start mass production of its Iron humanoid robot by the end of this year.

# NEURA Robotics Will Unveil Next-Generation Robots and Showcase the Neuraverse Platform at CES 2026

30 Dec 2025 | Published By [Dawn Zoldi](https://www.autonomyglobal.co/author/autonomy_jxp4njpy_global/ "Dawn Zoldi")

The Automatica-16.

**Las Vegas, USA/Metzingen, Germany: December 30, 2025** – NEURA Robotics, the pioneer in cognitive robotics and creator of the Neuraverse operating system, today announced that it will participate at CES 2026, taking place from January 6–9, 2026, at the Las Vegas Convention Center in Las Vegas, Nevada.

At CES 2026, NEURA Robotics will unveil the next generation of its humanoid robot, both in existing humanoid formats and new designs, marking a major expansion of its cognitive robotics portfolio.

...

January 6, 10:30 am – 11:15 am: David Reger and Spencer Huang, Product Lead for Robotics, NVIDIA (Guest)

January 8, 10:30 am – 11:15 am: David Reger and David Kehr, President Humanoid Robotics, Schaeffler Group USA, Inc (Guest)

January 9, 10:30 am – 11:00 am: David Reger

January 7, 10:00 – 10:40 am, David Reger joins CES conference session “Not Quite Human: How Humanoids Are Changing Work and Home Life”

Location: Las Vegas Convention Center, West Level 2, Room W219

For further information, images, and interview requests, please contact [neurarobotics@fgsglobal.com](mailto:neurarobotics@fgsglobal.com)

**About NEURA Robotics**

###### NEURA Robotics was founded in 2019 by David Reger with the mission to close key innovation gaps and usher in the era of cognitive robotics.
The award-winning innovators from Metzingen follow a consistent “one-device” approach across their entire product portfolio – from industrial to household robots. With the Neuraverse, the company is creating the foundation for the iPhone moment of robotics, bridging the gap between technology and humans. All core innovations, including AI, are developed in-house. NEURA’s cognitive robots can see, hear, and have a sense of touch. They act fully autonomously and learn from experience. Today, NEURA is on the path to bringing the first general-purpose humanoid robot to market, supported by a rapidly growing global partner network.

# BYD enters humanoid robot race with august debut

BYD is unveiling its humanoid robots this month, August 2026.

By Maria Mocerino

BYD enters humanoid robot race with august debut

BYD HAN (representational image). [BYD](http://www.byd.com/us)
Tesla’s biggest EV competitor BYD just revealed to the _South China Morning Post_ that the humanoids are coming in August at Di Space.

“Build Your Dreams” has, from meager battery manufacturing beginnings, become one of the world’s largest electric vehicle and clean technology companies.

From cars to buses, trucks to SUVs, BYU manufactures key components such as batteries and semiconductors, which has allowed them to dominate the market as they produce most of what they need in-house.

Whereas Tesla has emphasized software and autonomous driving, BYD has focused on manufacturing scale, battery technology, and a broad line-up of vehicles. And now – humanoids, just in time to take on Tesla’s Optimus.

BYD announced that they will unveil their robots at their designated showroom, Di Space, in an interactive exhibit. They clarified to _South China Morning Post_ that their humanoids will be functional. Attendees will be able to engage with the robots.

...

The excitement around this venture doesn’t surround the humanoids, but rather its manufacturing capabilities; its ability to produce humanoid robots at a scale that few companies can.

Li, BYD’s executive vice-president, also informed South China Morning Post that they believed that China would become the first market to “see full commercialisation of humanoid robots.” Given that Chinese companies are dominating the space right now, that belief appears well on its way to becoming a reality.

China sees robotics as a strategic industry, key for future economic growth.

## Manufacturing robots for manufacturers

Factory [automation](https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/us-ban-china-humanoid-robot-quadrupeds) is the first market. Humanoids could eventually perform tasks such as moving parts, assembling components, inspecting products, and handling materials. That would provide the company an additional advantage, able to test the robots before selling them to others.
If they become practical and usable, they could assist not only factories but also warehouses, hospitals, hotels, retail, construction, and eventually homes. Some believe this could become a trillion-dollar industry. Will AI become as transformative as EV? EV says yes.

BYD implied in their statement to _South China Morning Post_ that in a relatively short amount of time, they are past concept. They are ready to demonstrate their capacity to produce humanoids quickly.

“As BYD unveils its production model for humanoid robots, it will improve Chinese EV makers’ overall strength in this area,” said Ding Haifeng, a consultant at financial advisory firm Integrity in Shanghai, to _South Morning China [post](https://www.scmp.com/business/china-business/article/3362362/byd-debut-first-humanoid-robots-august-rivalry-tesla-intensifies?module=AI_Recommended_for_you_In-house&pgtype=section) ._
“The market will keep a close watch on other details like its production capacity and prices of the robots.”

As Tesla’s China president Allan Wang Hao said, they could “eventually manufacture humanoid robots,” as they haven’t successfully released Optimus into the commercial sector. And, with Xpend expected to unleash 1,000 robots upon us, we’ve officially entered the race to introduce humanoids into the labor force. Xpend expects that to happen in 2027. The race against Tesla is on. Even Musk believes that Tesla and China will meet head-to-head. They will dominate this market – first intending to address gaps in manufacturing.

Will AI take over that human job? Parts of it, at least.

The WeChat account of BYD's Di Space Zhengzhou venue posted a teaser poster of a humanoid robot on Saturday, hinting that the product will make its first public appearance in early August.

Notably, the account is a local channel for BYD's offline science education and experience venues, not the company's main official platform. BYD has yet to confirm the timing of the reveal or any product details.

"My goal is to put two or three robots in every store," Li said. Robots can explain products to customers, liven up the atmosphere, and even showcase vehicles.

Humanoid robots for households and the service industry will be a huge market for BYD, and robot sales consultants could become practical within the next year or two, she said.
Still, showroom robots cannot replace the "emotional connection" between human salespeople and customers, Li said. "We still need human employees, but robotics can help us improve our service further."

BYD also plans to build an open robot platform that will produce both its own in-house robots and products co-developed with other companies, she said.

William Li, founder, chairman, and CEO of Nio Inc (NYSE: NIO), said in March that the company would currently focus on selling more cars. Friday, August 7, 2026

# BYD unveils Xiao Di, its first humanoid robot

BYD

BYD publicly unveiled its first humanoid robot, named Xiao Di, at the Di Space brand-experience center in Zhengzhou in early August 2026, joining Tesla, Unitree, XPeng and Chery in the humanoid-robot race. The 1.61-meter, 58.5 kg robot has 31 degrees of freedom, translates between 6 Chinese dialects and 6 foreign languages in real time, and will begin greeting customers and demoing vehicles in Shenzhen and Shanghai showrooms before expanding to about 50 locations.
